en.one: Holding company owning Meritz Fire and Meritz Securities. It passed the quality walls; third-quarter profit fell 26.6%, so the price test depends on profit recovering.
en.business: Meritz Financial Group is a financial holding company. It owns all of the insurer Meritz Fire & Marine and the broker Meritz Securities; Meritz Capital is also in the group. The money comes from long-term health and protection insurance, from investing the insurance premiums, and from corporate finance and real estate lending. In the first nine months of 2026 consolidated net profit was 1.96 trillion won; 62% of profit came from insurance, 32% from the securities firm and 6% from Meritz Capital.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. Real return on equity averaged 18.6% over five years and was 15.8% in the weakest year. The part of the advantage that shows in numbers is the insurance book: at the end of June 2026 the contractual service margin (CSM) not yet booked as profit was 12.1 trillion won, and about 322 billion won of it moves into profit each quarter. The insurance licence and the agent network are a barrier to a newcomer. The weak side: insurance and corporate finance are businesses rivals can also do; the advantage rests on pricing discipline and management more than on a brand. A large part of profit depends on investment income; in the third quarter losses on shares cut the insurer's profit by 29.2%.
en.mgmt: The largest shareholder is Cho Jung-ho with 10 related parties: 56.13% (end of 2025). The National Pension Service holds 6.51%. Profit returns to shareholders through buybacks: between March 2023 and March 2026 the company bought back and cancelled 3.09 trillion won of shares (36 million shares, about 17.7% of those issued). In 2025 the share returned to shareholders was 61.7% of profit. The company puts all of the money into buybacks and cancellation rather than a cash dividend; a new 700 billion won programme began in March 2026. Note: the holding company's investment in subsidiaries relative to its own equity (double leverage) rose from 112.1% in March 2026 to 127.8% in June 2026.
en.latest: 11 November 2026: Consolidated net profit in the third quarter was 490.5 billion won (668.4 billion a year earlier; −26.6%). Nine-month profit was 1.96 trillion won (−3.2%). The reason: lower investment income because of stock market volatility; Meritz Fire's quarterly profit was 328.5 billion won (−29.2%). Insurance profit, however, rose 7.6% in nine months (1.10 trillion won). Meritz Securities' nine-month profit was 720.5 billion won (+12.0%). The return on equity the company reports is 23.5% and the solvency ratio (K-ICS) 225.7%. The figures are from press reports; the company's own document could not be read yet.
risks: The price test rests on the last 12 months' profit and on past growth; profit fell 26.6% in the third quarter and nine-month profit is 3.2% below last year. If investment income does not recover, the earnings and growth in the calculation are too high.
Real estate lending is large: 29.5 trillion won in June 2026 (25.9 trillion in Korea), more than twice equity. In the second quarter the group set aside a net 187.5 billion won of provisions.
The Homeplus loan is still open: provisions against the existing loans are about 240 billion won, and the company has made a new loan as well.
Regulation affects profit directly: a higher education tax, a cap on agent commissions and rules on insurance assumptions came into force in 2026.
Control sits with one family (56.13%), and the double leverage ratio rose to 127.8% while the holding company kept buying back shares; if dividends from subsidiaries fall, the pace of buybacks slows.

en.one: One of Korea's large independent insurance agencies. It passed the quality walls; the advantage rests on a sales force that must be re-recruited every year, and commission rules are changing. The moat is weak.
en.business: INCAR Financial Service is an independent agency (GA) in Korea that sells the policies of many insurers. It earns sales commissions from the insurers and pays most of them on to its own agents. In the first half of 2026 revenue was 640 billion won (+36.5%) and net profit 44.5 billion won (+34.8%). The number of agents rose from 20,651 at the end of 2025 to 24,724 at the end of June.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak. The advantage comes from scale: 24,724 agents, a five-year average real return on equity of 37.4% and 29.7% in the lowest year. But this scale is won anew every year. The agents are not employees; they are recruited with settlement bonuses and can leave. Agent retention fell from 83.1% to 79.3%. In July 2026 the cap on first-year commissions (the 1200% rule) began to apply to what agencies pay their own agents; from January 2027 commissions will be spread over four years, and from 2029 over seven. The rules limit the tools an agency uses to attract agents, and the insurers' own sales forces are growing too (+11.7%). Profit is booked on an accrual basis: commissions paid in advance to agents (prepaid expenses) stand at 781.5 billion won, more than nine times annual profit; operating cash flow in the first half was minus 27.6 billion won. An advantage that has to be defended anew every year does not count as a moat in this filter.
en.mgmt: Founder and chairman Choi Byung-chae and related parties held 43.37% of the shares at the end of 2025. The company paid a dividend of 370 won a share for 2025 (2024: 100 won, 2023: 350 won). It cancelled 2,116,143 treasury shares in December 2025 and signed a 7 billion won buyback contract in June 2026. Flaws: the chairman and the president have borrowed against their shares (2,651,801 of the president's shares are pledged), and the company paid an administrative fine to the regulator after its 2024 inspection. Most of the profit stays in the company and goes into enlarging the agent force.
en.latest: 14 August 2026: In the first half revenue was 640 billion won (+36.5%), operating profit 58.3 billion won (+30.1%) and net profit 44.5 billion won (+34.8%). Second-quarter net profit was 22.0 billion won, against 22.5 billion in the first quarter. The company put the fall down to about 6 billion won of one-off costs: an administrative fine and the cost of a golf tournament. The third-quarter report had not been published on 13 November 2026.
risks: Commission rules are changing: from January 2027 sales commissions will be spread over four years, and from 2029 over seven. This changes the timing of revenue and cash; the effect on profit is not yet known.
Commissions paid in advance to agents stand at 781.5 billion won on the balance sheet. If policies lapse early or new sales slow, this asset is written off as expense.
Agents can leave: retention fell from 83.1% to 79.3%, and insurers are enlarging their own sales forces quickly.
Operating cash flow in the first half was minus 27.6 billion won; profit is not turning into cash.
The chairman and the president have borrowed against their shares; if the price falls, pledged shares could be sold.

en.one: Maker of acne patches and wound dressings. It passed the quality walls; it failed Wall 3 because more than half of sales depend on one US customer.
en.business: T&L (티앤엘) makes hydrocolloid wound dressings and acne patches, mostly for other companies' brands. In the first half of 2026 revenue was 101.1 billion won; 79.7 billion of it came from hydrocolloid products and 78.1 billion from exports. Sales to the United States were 57.4 billion won. The plants are in Yongin and Anseong.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from manufacturing know-how and scale, and it shows in the numbers: real return on equity averaged 20.4% over five years and was 15.7% in the weakest year; the operating margin in the first half of 2026 was 42.8%. The weak side is large: the brand belongs to the customer, not to the company. A single customer gave 56% of revenue in the first half of 2026 (56.7 billion won; 45% in 2025, 58% in 2024). Broker reports identify this customer as Church & Dwight, owner of the Mighty Patch brand. The same reports say that since the second quarter of 2025 the customer orders when its stock runs down instead of on a regular schedule. When the customer cut inventory in 2025, US sales fell 27% and net profit fell 18%. The company therefore did not pass criterion E (dependence on a single customer).
en.mgmt: The largest shareholder is Choi Yun-so (23.70%); Choi Hyeon-jun holds 11.23%. A dividend of 1,500 won a share was paid from 2025 profit (750 won the year before), 12.0 billion won in total. Between September 2025 and September 2026 the company bought back 7.2 billion won of shares (143,491 shares); no cancellation has been announced, and the company says it may keep them for acquisitions and employee awards. A bonus issue was made in August 2026 (7,942,120 new shares; the share count became 16,070,120). There is almost no debt: cash and short-term financial assets are 104.2 billion won against total liabilities of 29.0 billion. With the related company Cosmeditech there were, in 2025, an asset sale of 5.8 billion won, outsourcing purchases of 7.8 billion and a loan of 2.0 billion.
en.latest: 14 August 2026: The company published its half-year report (a correction to the notes followed on 21 August). Second-quarter revenue was 56.0 billion won (38.8 billion a year earlier), operating profit 25.0 billion won (10.0 billion a year earlier) and net profit 19.9 billion won (7.8 billion a year earlier). First-half revenue was 101.1 billion won (+12%) and net profit 36.4 billion won (+54%). The second quarter of last year was weak because the customer was cutting inventory. The third-quarter report is due by 14 November 2026; it had not been published when this report was written.
risks: The profit of the last 12 months rests on one customer's orders: it gave 56% of first-half revenue. When the customer cut inventory in 2025 net profit fell 18%; if that happens again, profit and the calculated margin fall together.
The brand is in the customer's hands. If the customer finds a second manufacturer or takes production in-house, the filings show no contract that would prevent it.
77% of sales are exports. A stronger won or higher US tariffs would narrow the margin; first-half profit includes 3.2 billion won of currency gains.
The 44.6% operating margin of the second quarter is very high even by the company's own history; a broker estimate expects lower sales and margin in the third quarter.
There are asset sales, outsourcing purchases and loans with the related company Cosmeditech; this is something a minority shareholder should follow.

en.one: Seller of MLB and Discovery branded apparel. Passed the quality walls; failed the management test: much profit is tied up in a non-core golf fund.
en.business: F&F designs and sells clothing, caps and shoes under the MLB and Discovery Expedition brands; production is outsourced. In 2025 revenue was 1.934 trillion won and operating profit 468.5 billion won (a 24.2% margin). About half of revenue comes from China (960 billion won in 2025). The MLB brand does not belong to the company; it is used under licence. The company bought the Discovery Expedition trademark in August 2026 for 80 million dollars.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage shows in the numbers: the operating margin was 23.8% in 2024 and 24.2% in 2025; real return on equity averaged 30.5% over five years and was 20.4% in its lowest year. That margin is high for an apparel company and shows pricing power. The weak side: the largest brand, MLB, is rented, not owned; we could not find the licence term or expiry date in the documents read in this run. Earnings depend on China, and growth there has stopped: the Chinese subsidiary's revenue fell 4% in the third quarter of 2026. Real return on equity has come down from 51.8% in 2021 to the 20-25% range.
en.mgmt: The company did not pass this test (D = 0). Control lies with F&F Holdings and parties acting with it: 62.8%; the free float is 35.0%. Only a small part of profit is paid out: the 2025 dividend was 2,700 won a share, 69.3 billion won in total, against profit of 401 billion won. In 2021, 558 billion won went into the Centroid private equity fund that bought the golf equipment maker TaylorMade. The carrying amount of this stake was 718.9 billion won at the end of June 2026: 27.6% of total assets. This is a large financial investment outside the main business, and it also moves reported profit (90 billion won of equity-method income in 2025). The company is now examining a purchase of all of TaylorMade; the price being discussed is around 2.5 billion dollars, more than the company's own market value. Over five years about 85% of profit stayed in the company, while real earnings per share did not grow.
en.latest: 10 November 2026: Preliminary third-quarter results were announced. Revenue was 452.1 billion won (−4.7%), operating profit 108.4 billion won (−15.3%) and net profit attributable to owners 65.9 billion won (−32.9%). The Chinese subsidiary's revenue was 272.4 billion won (−4%): retail sales were flat and an inventory adjustment reduced shipments. The company has begun due diligence on TaylorMade; a decision is expected by the end of the year, or early 2027 at the latest. The detailed quarterly report had not been published when this was written.
risks: Profit for the last 12 months looks higher than what the main business earns: net profit attributable to owners was 492 billion won, while operating profit was 481 billion won. Most of the gap is income booked from the TaylorMade fund; if the fund is sold, or the company buys TaylorMade, that income goes away. Net profit fell 32.9% in the third quarter.
The MLB brand is rented. If the licence is not renewed, or its terms get heavier, most of the business is affected; the term and expiry date were not in the documents we read.
If TaylorMade is bought, the company will have taken on, with debt, a business larger than its own market value, and one unrelated to apparel.
About half of revenue comes from China. If demand or the exchange rate turns there, profit falls; shipments to China have been weak for two quarters in 2026.
The company is listed in Korea but earns half its revenue in China; the inflation adjustment was made with Korean inflation.

en.one: A shipyard building mid-size crude oil tankers. Passed the quality walls; work is won by bidding, the high margin is recent. Eliminated at Wall 3.
en.business: Daehan Shipbuilding (대한조선) builds mid-size tankers at its single yard in Haenam, South Korea. Its main product is the 157,000-tonne Suezmax crude oil tanker; it earns its money as it builds the ship, from the instalments the shipowner pays. At the end of September 2026 the order book held 35 ships worth 3.3 billion dollars: 30 Suezmax tankers, 3 shuttle tankers and 2 container ships. Revenue in 2025 was 1,228.1 billion won and operating profit 294.1 billion won.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak. The advantage is real: the yard builds the same ship type again and again, and the operating margin has been above 20% for eight quarters (25.3% in the third quarter of 2026). But ship orders are won by bidding and the price is set by the world newbuilding market; today's margin rests on deliveries of orders taken at high prices in 2024. The record is also short: the source has return on equity for only three fiscal years (21.1%, 52.4% and 29.2% in real terms; 30.6% in the last 12 months). According to the figures in a broker report, the operating margin was about 4% in 2023. This filter does not count as a moat an advantage that has not been proven through a downturn; the company was eliminated at Wall 3 because its B score is 1.
en.mgmt: The largest shareholder is KHI: it bought the company in 2022 with a consortium and held 46.7% in mid-2026. The shares were listed on 1 August 2025; the listed history is a little over one year. A small part of profit is paid out: in March 2026 shares worth 40 billion won were bought back and cancelled, and 9.6 billion won of dividends were paid. On 10 November 2026 the company pledged to return at least 30% of annual consolidated net profit for 2027-2029 and approved a new 10 billion won buyback. KHI's former sister company K Shipbuilding is up for sale; according to the press, KHI plans to sell its stake there as well.
en.latest: 11 November 2026: Third-quarter revenue was 327.7 billion won (+19.6%), operating profit 82.7 billion won (+24.4%) and net profit 36.9 billion won (−43.9%; 65.8 billion a year earlier). According to the press, a foreign exchange loss pulled net profit down (44.7 billion won in the quarter). Nine-month net profit was 193.0 billion won (+13.5%) and operating profit 260.6 billion won (+31.1%). The figures are preliminary and unaudited. Orders for 17 Suezmax tankers worth 1.5 billion dollars were won during the year; the annual target was exceeded by 62%. On 12 November 2026 an order for two more tankers worth 249.8 billion won was announced (delivery by June 2030).
risks: Profit depends on the cycle: today's margin comes from orders taken at high prices in 2024. If newbuilding prices or tanker demand fall, the margin on deliveries a few years out falls too.
One yard, one main product: 30 of the 35 ships in the order book are Suezmax tankers.
Revenue is in dollars and costs are in won: profit falls when the exchange rate falls. In the third quarter net profit dropped 43.9% because of a foreign exchange loss.

The record is short: the shares were listed in August 2025 and the source has return on equity for only three fiscal years. The other shipyard of the controlling shareholder KHI changed hands; the group's need for cash could affect minority shareholders.

en.one: Maker of the Oligio skin-tightening device. It did not pass the moat test: advertising tripled, operating profit fell, and a third of 12-month profit is a non-cash derivative gain.
en.business: Wontech sells radio-frequency and laser devices to skin clinics; its best-known product is the Oligio skin-tightening device. The money comes from device sales and from the tips used up in each treatment. In 2025 revenue was 156.8 billion won and operating profit 51.7 billion won; 37.6% of revenue came from radio-frequency and ultrasound devices, 31.5% from lasers and 24.1% from consumable tips. In the first nine months of 2026, 75.4% of revenue came from abroad; the largest market is Thailand.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. There is an advantage: real return on equity was between 21.4% and 45.0% in the last five readings, and consumable tips are a quarter of revenue. But in 2026 that advantage is being defended at a high cost. In the first half revenue rose 13.6%, selling and administrative costs rose 79% (advertising went from 4.3 billion won to 13.2 billion won) and operating profit fell 30% (from 31.8 billion won to 22.3 billion won). The third-quarter operating margin was about 15% (33% in 2025). The product is sold in a crowded field with established brands such as Thermage and Korean rivals; the US and China subsidiaries had lost their capital as of the third quarter of 2025, and Oligio's approval in China has been pending for four years. No market share figure was found in the documents. The brand has not yet shown that it can hold its price without rising advertising spend.
en.mgmt: The founding Kim family runs the company (two co-chief executives: Kim Jong-won and Kim Jung-hyun); ownership percentages could not be read from a company document in this run. Capital allocation is mixed. On the positive side: three share cancellations in 2026 (1,891,516 shares in total) and buyback contracts of 11 billion won. On the negative side: in May 2026 the company issued a 75 billion won zero-coupon convertible bond (conversion price 8,270 won, about 10.1% of shares; the price can reset down to 5,789 won); the share trades at 3,530 won today. In the same year the company is both buying back shares and issuing a dilutive bond. It agreed to buy land and a building for a head office in Gwacheon for 244.5 billion won; that is 112.5% of total assets at the end of 2025. A stake purchase in Japan was disclosed about four months late; the exchange signalled a possible unfaithful-disclosure designation. In September 2026 it bought 39.03% of loss-making Won Medico for 13.3 billion won. The share count rose 24% in five years. Share-based pay, goodwill and pension obligations: looked for, but could not be read because the company document could not be opened.
en.latest: 13 November 2026: Third-quarter revenue was about 36.2 billion won, operating profit about 5.5 billion won (margin about 15%) and the net result a loss of 2.85 billion won. The company attributed the loss to a non-cash valuation loss from exchange rates. Nine-month revenue was about 124.0 billion won (+12.2%); overseas revenue rose 31.6%. First-half net profit was 25.9 billion won (+22.6%), but it includes a non-cash derivative gain of 21.2 billion won linked to the convertible bond; operating cash flow in the same period was minus 13.4 billion won. Figures are from press reports; the company's own document could not be opened.
risks: Profit for the last 12 months overstates the earning power of the business: first-half net profit of 25.9 billion won includes a non-cash derivative gain of 21.2 billion won (pre-tax); the third quarter closed with a loss.
Advertising and selling costs are growing much faster than revenue; operating cash flow turned negative in the first half (receivables rose 14.2 billion won, inventories 7.9 billion won).
The 244.5 billion won head office commitment is larger than total assets; 80% of the payment falls due at completion in 2032.
The 75 billion won convertible bond can dilute shares by about 10%; investors can demand repayment from May 2028.
Three quarters of revenue comes from abroad and is concentrated in Thailand; exchange differences move profit from quarter to quarter.

Kâr temettüye ve satın almaya gidiyor: hisse başına temettü 2022'de 75, 2023'te 100, 2024'te 200 won; dağıtım oranı %21-33. Mart 2024'te Devenish, Ocak 2026'da Biomatrix ve Nutribins alındı. en.one: Maker of feed additives and piglet feed; it bought US-based Devenish with debt in 2024. It did not pass the moat test: margin is around 10% and there is no market share evidence.
en.business: Easy Bio makes animal feed additives and piglet feed. About 74.8% of revenue comes from feed additives and 25.2% from compound feed. In March 2024 it bought US-based Devenish Nutrition, which was larger than itself; revenue went from about 165 billion won to 384 billion won in 2024 and the overseas share passed 60%. In 2025 revenue was about 477 billion won and operating profit about 45 billion won (margin 9.4%). In the first half of 2026 revenue was 278.8 billion won and operating profit 28.3 billion won.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. There is an advantage: customers are reluctant to switch specialty feed additives, and additive margins are several times those of ordinary feed (2-3%). But the numbers do not prove a narrow moat. Consolidated operating margin was 10.4% in 2022, 12.5% in 2023, 8.4% in 2024 and 9.4% in 2025: not high, and it fell with the acquisition. No market share figure appears in any document read. In compound feed about 80% of cost is grain; the price is passed on to customers, but this is a commodity business. Part of the high return on equity (latest real reading 34.3%) comes from debt: at the end of 2024 liabilities were about three times equity, and return on invested capital stayed in the 14-17% range. Growth came through acquisitions; Devenish's margin was around 4% before the purchase.
en.mgmt: The main shareholder is Easy Holdings with three related persons: 51.53%. The company was formed by a split from Easy Holdings in 2020; the group's chicken, duck and pig farms are its customers, so there are related-party sales (the amount could not be read). Profit goes to dividends and acquisitions: dividend per share was 75 won in 2022, 100 in 2023 and 200 in 2024; the payout ratio was 21-33%. It bought Devenish in March 2024 and Biomatrix and Nutribins in January 2026. The purchases are related to the main business but were made with debt: net debt/EBITDA is 2.07 according to the source. Goodwill relative to equity, share-based pay and off-balance-sheet obligations: looked for, but could not be read because the company document could not be opened.
en.latest: 14 August 2026: In the second quarter revenue was 148.1 billion won, operating profit 15.1 billion won and net profit 10.9 billion won (a year earlier 113.8 billion, 11.0 billion and 4.1 billion won). First-half operating profit was 28.3 billion won (20.1 billion a year earlier; +41%). Figures are from a data site; third-quarter results could not be found in this run.
risks: Debt is high: on the end-2025 estimate, liabilities are about 2.3 times equity; interest and exchange rates affect profit directly.

Most of the profit now comes from the United States; the inflation adjustment uses Korean inflation, and US herd sizes and tariffs move the results (weakness was seen in the second and third quarters of 2025).
Growth relies on acquisitions; the amount of goodwill could not be read.

en.one: Builds and maintains corporate networks with Cisco equipment. It did not pass the moat test: work is won by bidding and the operating margin is 6%.
en.business: OPASnet builds computer networks for companies and public bodies and then maintains them. Most of the equipment comes from Cisco; the company has been a Cisco Gold partner since 2011. In 2025 revenue was 233.3 billion won, operating profit 14.0 billion won and net profit attributable to owners 12.7 billion won. Network construction revenue was 137.1 billion won (+21.5%) and maintenance revenue 82.8 billion won (+24.9%; 35.6% of revenue). Customers include SK Telecom, Samsung SDS, financial institutions and public bodies.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. The business is installing and selling equipment made by someone else; projects are won by bids and tenders. The numbers show it: in 2025 gross margin was 17.2% and operating margin 6.0% (5.5% in 2024). There are rivals doing the same work (Insung Information, S-Net). What could count as an advantage: the Cisco Gold certification and recurring maintenance work on installed networks, which is more than a third of revenue. These set the company apart from a pure tender business, but pricing power does not show in the margins and there is dependence on a single supplier. Real return on equity averaged 17.5% over five years; that is the result of a service business that runs on little capital rather than of a moat.
en.mgmt: Chief executive Jang Su-hyun owns 25.29%; with related persons 41.30%. Other large holders are Kim Yoon-jung with 7.41% and Park Geon-sang with 7.17%. The company has net cash (net debt/EBITDA of -2.73 in the source). Profit has started to return to owners: dividend per share was 100 won in 2024 and 250 won in 2025. No large investment outside the main business and no share issuance were seen. Share-based pay, goodwill and off-balance-sheet obligations: looked for, but could not be read because the company document could not be opened.
en.latest: 14 August 2026: In the second quarter revenue was 47.3 billion won, operating profit 1.9 billion won and net profit 3.6 billion won (a year earlier 58.2 billion, 5.6 billion and 4.6 billion won).
